implementation_notes: TypeScript changes nothing about the runtime: the competing-consumer realization is still a queue library (BullMQ workers over Redis, a kafkajs group member, an SQS consumer) in which several workers pull from one queue. Types are the contribution - give the payload one discriminated-union Job type and instantiate Worker<Job, Result, 'emails'> so every worker in the pool parses the same shape, and keep the handlers total with an exhaustive switch. The type system can pin the payload but not the delivery count, so idempotency stays a runtime property.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: broker clients hand handlers parsed JSON, so validate (zod/io-ts) at the boundary unless you trust every producer's build.
Two worker builds from different commits can disagree on the payload shape while both type-check - version the job contract like an API.
Casting job.data 'as any' (or a shared permissive helper) defeats the exhaustiveness check that makes the pool safe to evolve.

variants.name: Typed Kafka consumer group member
variants.implementation_notes: The broker-level realization with types: each group member owns a set of partitions and processes their messages with a typed payload, and the rebalance protocol decides which member owns which point-to-point channel. Model each topic's message as a discriminated union, decode with a schema validator before the switch, and let the group mechanism - not application code - distribute partitions between the competing members.
pitfalls: Partition ownership is rebalanced away at any time: handler state tied to a partition (in-memory caches, offsets in variables) must be rebuilt.
Runtime validation is not optional - kafkajs consumers receive bytes, and a type assertion on JSON.parse is a claim, not a check.
